NONE: › to do something or go somewhere very slowly, taking more time than is necessary

example: Stop dawdling! You'll be late for school!
別磨蹭了！你上學遲到了！

NONE: B2 the period in the day when light from the sun begins to appear in the sky
› the start of a period of time or the beginning of something new

I: › If a day or period of time dawns, it begins.
› mainly UK to become known or obvious
見分曉，水落石出；變得明朗

example: We woke at dawn.
天一亮我們就醒了。
We left as dawn was breaking (= starting).
我們離開時天將破曉。
We left at the break of dawn.
我們離開時天將破曉。
The fall of the Berlin Wall marked the dawn of a new era in European history.
柏林牆的倒塌標誌著歐洲歷史上一個新紀元的開始。
We worked from dawn to dusk, seven days a week.
我們從早到晚地工作，一週七天都是如此。
He left the house just as the day was dawning.
天將破曉時他離開了那座房子。
In the late 1970s, the personal computer era was dawning.
個人電腦時代開始於20世紀70年代晚期。
Gradually the truth about him dawned.
他的真實面目漸漸暴露了出來。
[ + that ] It eventually dawned that he wouldn't be coming back.
最終證明他不會回來了。

NONE: › the singing of birds together just before dawn
C2 If a fact dawns on you, you understand it after a period of not understanding it.

example: [ + that ] I was about to pay for the shopping when it suddenly dawned on me that I'd left my wallet at home.
我買完東西要付錢時，才突然發現我把錢包留在家裡了。

NONE: › starting to happen or become obvious

example: There is a dawning realization that we cannot continue to deplete the planet.
人們越來越意識到不能繼續無休止地消耗地球上的資源了。
